title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 233
paragraphs: Moreover, the answer given by the Oracle of Ammon also bears witness in support of my opinion that Egypt is of the extent I declare it to be in my account; and I heard of this answer after I had already formed my own opinion about Egypt. The people of the cities of Marea and Apis, dwelling in those parts of Egypt that border on Libya, held themselves to be Libyans and not Egyptians, and also being burdened by the rules of religious service — because they wished not to be debarred from the use of cows' flesh — sent to Ammon saying they had nothing in common with the Egyptians, for they dwelt outside the Delta and agreed with them in nothing; and they said they desired that it might be lawful for them to eat everything without distinction. The god, however, did not permit them to do so, but answered that Egypt was that land which the Nile comes over and waters, and that those were Egyptians who, dwelling below the city of Elephantine, drank of that river. Thus it was answered to them by the Oracle about this:
